newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-CREW WINS SEVENTH STRAIGHT, JOINS PLAYOFF CHASE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CREW WINS SEVENTH STRAIGHT, JOINS PLAYOFF CHASE.

text.p: The Columbus Crew, longshots to reach the Major League Soccer playoffs one month ago, continued their remarkable comeback with a seventh consecutive win, a 5-1 victory over the Kansas City Wiz on Saturday.
Under interim coach Tom Fitzgerald, the fifth-place Crew (13-16, 31 points) moved into the Eastern Conference playoff race.
U.S. Olympic midfielder Brian Maisonneuve, who entered the match with only two goals, scored three times as the surging Crew upended the Wiz, who lead the league with 61 goals.
Marcelo Carrera and Pete Marino also had goals. Preki tallied his 18th goal for the Wiz (17-14, 45), in first place in the Western Conference.
The top four teams in each of the two five-team conferences qualify for the playoffs, which begin on September 25. Each team plays 32 regular-season games.
The New England Revolution (15-14, 33) moved into a third-place tie with the New York/New Jersey MetroStars after a pair of victories over the Dallas Burn (16-13, 40).

On Wednesday, U.S. international Joe-Max Moore converted a penalty kick in the 78th minute to lift the Revolution to a 2-1 victory against the Burn, who had tied the game on Ted Eck's goal only four minutes earlier.
On Sunday, New England registered a 2-0 victory in Dallas. Darren Sawatzky and U.S. Olympian Imad Baba scored in the first half, as goalkeeper Aidan Heaney recorded the shutout.

The MetroStars (13-15, 33) split their two games. In a lacklustre performance, they dropped a 2-0 decision to the Eastern Conference leaders, the Tampa Bay Mutiny (16-12, 48), in East Rutherford, New Jersey on Wednesday.

Roy Lassiter, who leads the league with 22 goals, and U.S. Olympic defender Frank Hedjuk each scored for Tampa Bay, which clinched at least a second-place finish. The Mutiny played without injured Italian forward Giuseppe Galderisi and Colombian international midfielder Carlos Valderrama, who had commitments back home.

The MetroStars bounced back with a 2-1 victory over second-place D.C. United (14-15, 40) on Friday, as Colombian Antony De Avila and U.S. Olympian A.J. Wood scored first-half goals. Tony Sanneh scored for United.

The San Jose Clash (14-14, 38) qualified for the playoffs without playing, as the Colorado Rapids (11-20, 29), stuck in last place in the Western Conference with the worst record in the league, defeated the Los Angeles Galaxy (16-12, 40) in a shootout 1-0 in Pasadena, California, on Thursday.
Jean Harbour and Scott Benedetti converted their shootout attempts for Colorado, which needed a three-point regulation victory and not a one-point shootout win to keep its slim playoff hopes alive.

On Sunday, Missael Espinoza scored two goals and assisted on Paul Bravo's insurance goal, as the Clash defeated the Rapids 3-1 in Denver. Harbour scored off a 30-yard free kick for Colorado, which played its home season finale.
